affectedSurfaces: kota report CLI and JSON output
hypothesis: An operator-only supervision-load section will make concurrent autonomy workstreams and human-action pressure visible without changing dispatch, prompts, or reviewer pass/fail behavior.

metricsCompared.name: focused supervision-load report tests
metricsCompared.baseline: autonomy reports had no supervision-load aggregation, rendered section, or focused CLI/JSON coverage
metricsCompared.candidate: focused report tests cover normal load, overloaded load, pending-merge pressure, missing/unreadable evidence, multi-scope grouping, rendered output, and JSON output

metricsCompared.name: operator-visible load evidence
metricsCompared.baseline: operators had to inspect active runs, task claims, approvals, owner questions, dead letters, and attention items as separate surfaces
metricsCompared.candidate: report transcript and JSON artifact expose bounded counts, status, thresholds, unknown evidence, workstreams, and top references together

metricsCompared.name: autonomy execution posture
metricsCompared.baseline: no dispatch gate used operator supervision load as autonomy input
metricsCompared.candidate: the new signal remains in operator report aggregation and rendering only, with no agent prompt or queue-shaping path added

rationale: The reviewer-class change is limited to operator reporting: it reuses existing runtime artifacts and review-scrutiny counts, reports missing stores as unknown evidence, and leaves workflow dispatch and agent prompts unchanged. The focused tests and captured report artifacts prove the operator-visible behavior while the repair split keeps the implementation under the source-size guideline.
